Motion designers, I'm sorry.

I asked Claude Opus 5.5 for a showreel as if it were applying for a motion design job, and it made this from one prompt without After Effects or stock music, writing every frame in code and the soundtrack in Python.

Would you hire it? https://t.co/reu4cJmc9W

and most of it is noise.


      
      
        Over a thousand new AI papers land every week, and the labs ship on top of that. A week of AI research is more than a person can read in a month.


        A few of those papers will change how you work. Telling those from the rest takes reading them, which is the thing there was never time for.

      Asked, answered.

      
        
          How is this different from AI newsletters?
          The Attention Layer is a weekly magazine, not a newsletter. Most newsletters cover a handful of papers picked from the week. This goes through everything published — over a thousand cs.AI papers — and writes up the few that earn it.

        
        
          Can I trust machine-written analysis?
          Every number in an issue links to the table it came from, so you can check any claim in place.

        
        
          Who is it for?
          AI researchers and engineers who act on papers — people who cite this work or build on it. Stories assume you know the field.

        
        
          What's free?
          A set of issues from the archive stays open to everyone, marked on the shelf above. Recent issues are for members.

        
        
          How do I cancel?
          One click from your account. Access runs to the end of the period you paid for.
